exception_message: [LOGIC] I2-051-ShipShape/sh:sparql: The SPARQL constraint rejects every positive-shear case whose position lies between 0.6 LUI and 0.9 LUI unless Cf is exactly 0 or 1, although the requirement specifies Cf only for the aft-through-0.6 LUI interval and the 0.9-LUI-through-forward interval and imposes no Cf value in the intervening interval. Required change: Do not produce a violation solely because a positive-shear position is in the unspecified 0.6-to-0.9 LUI interval; enforce the Cf boundary values only within their explicitly specified intervals, while retaining FI = Cf × FIB for positive-shear cases. | [CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY] I2-051-ShipShape/nltl:hasCalculationCase/[nltl:shearForceDirection]: The direction value is constrained only by cardinality, so an arbitrary resource or literal can be supplied; the SPARQL formula is then skipped unless the value happens to equal nltl:positiveShearForce, allowing an invalid direction value to bypass the positive-shear applicability condition. Required change: Constrain nltl:shearForceDirection values to the canonical shearForceDirectionValue class, while retaining the conditional formula enforcement only for nltl:positiveShearForce.
source_oracle_rationale: Interpolated positive-shear distribution factor is numerically wrong.

Node ex:ship must conform to one or more shapes in [ sh:property [ sh:datatype xsd:boolean ; sh:hasValue Literal("false" = False, datatype=xsd:boolean) ; sh:maxCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:minCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:path nltl:beamTheoryUsed ] ] , [ sh:property [ sh:datatype xsd:boolean ; sh:hasValue Literal("true" = True, datatype=xsd:boolean) ; sh:maxCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:minCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:path nltl:beamTheoryUsed ], [ sh:maxCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:minCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:node [ sh:property [ sh:datatype xsd:decimal ; sh:maxCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:minCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:path qudt:numericValue ], [ sh:hasValue <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/MegaPA> ; sh:maxCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:minCount Literal("1", datatype=xsd:integer) ; sh:path qudt:unit ] ] ; sh:path nltl:allowableShearStress ] ; sh:sparql [ sh:message Literal("Allowable shear stress must be no greater than 0.9 times the yield shear stress when beam theory is used.") ; sh:select Literal("
                    PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
                    PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
                    PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
                    SELECT $this
                    WHERE {
                        $this nltl:beamTheoryUsed true ;
                              nltl:yieldPoint ?yieldPointNode ;
                              nltl:allowableShearStress ?allowableNode .
                        ?yieldPointNode qudt:numericValue ?yieldPoint .
                        ?allowableNode qudt:numericValue ?allowable .
                        FILTER (?allowable > (0.9 * (?yieldPoint / 1.7320508075688772)))
                    }
                ") ] ]

exception_message: [THRESHOLD] gs:TRF049_FrameShape SPARQL constraint with message "Each installed bracket must be at least as thick as the frame web, with a stiffened edge against buckling.": The constraint cannot detect a bracket thinner than the frame web: its outer FILTER NOT EXISTS requires that no valid frame thickness exists, while its inner FILTER EXISTS simultaneously requires a valid frame thickness. Consequently, a bracket with bracketValue < frameValue is accepted whenever the frame thickness is valid. Required change: Replace the contradictory filters with logic that rejects an installed bracket when no valid frame thickness exists or when any bracket thickness is less than the frame web thickness, while preserving the existing stiffening requirements and inclusive greater-than-or-equal threshold. | [LOGIC] gs:TRF049_FrameShape SPARQL constraint with message "A frame running through a supporting structure must provide a valid integer web-plate connection side count of exactly 2 and must connect both sides of its web plate to the relevant supporting structure.": The connection test verifies only one generic frame-attachment link reciprocated by the supporting structure. It does not identify or require two distinct web-plate sides, nor evidence that each side is connected by direct welding, a collar plate, or a lug. A single connection can therefore satisfy the constraint while the other web-plate side is unconnected. Required change: Represent and require two distinct side-specific connection records or equivalent evidence, with both sides linked to the relevant supporting structure and each connection identified as direct welding, collar plate, or lug. | [CARDINALITY] _:TRF049_WithinIceTrue / gs:TRF049_FrameShape side-count logic: webPlateConnectionSideCount has no SHACL datatype or cardinality constraint. The SPARQL condition accepts a frame if it has any one xsd:integer value equal to 2, even when additional side-count values are also present, so the modeled count is not constrained to exactly one value of exactly 2. Required change: Add a property constraint for nltl:webPlateConnectionSideCount requiring exactly one xsd:integer value with sh:hasValue 2, or enforce the equivalent exact-cardinality condition in SPARQL.

sh:sparql [ sh:message Literal("Spindle torque factor and torque results must satisfy the declared blade-failure formula.") ; sh:select Literal("
                    PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
                    PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
                    PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
                    SELECT $this
                    WHERE {
                        $this nltl:bladeExpandedAreaRatio ?earNode ;
                              nltl:propellerBladeCount ?z ;
                              nltl:leadingEdgeChordPortionAtZeroPointEightRadius ?leNode ;
                              nltl:trailingEdgeChordPortionAtZeroPointEightRadius ?teNode ;
                              nltl:extremeIceForce ?forceNode ;
                              nltl:bladeFailureSpindleTorqueFactor ?factorNode ;
                              nltl:bladeFailureSpindleTorque ?failureNode ;
                              nltl:maximumSpindleTorque ?maximumNode .
                        ?earNode qudt:numericValue ?ear .
                        ?leNode qudt:numericValue ?le .
                        ?teNode qudt:numericValue ?te .
                        ?forceNode qudt:numericValue ?force .
                        ?factorNode qudt:numericValue ?factor .
                        ?failureNode qudt:numericValue ?failure .
                        ?maximumNode qudt:numericValue ?maximum .
                        BIND((4.0 * ?ear) / xsd:decimal(?z) AS ?ratio)
                        BIND(0.7 * (1.0 - (?ratio * ?ratio * ?ratio)) AS ?rawFactor)
                        BIND(IF(?rawFactor < 0.3, 0.3, ?rawFactor) AS ?expectedFactor)
                        BIND(IF(?le > (0.8 * ?te), ?le, (0.8 * ?te)) AS ?chord)
                        BIND(?chord * ?expectedFactor * ?force AS ?expectedTorque)
                        BIND((ABS(?expectedFactor) * 0.000001) + 0.000000001 AS ?factorTolerance)
                        BIND((ABS(?expectedTorque) * 0.000001) + 0.000000001 AS ?torqueTolerance)
                        FILTER(
                            ABS(?factor - ?expectedFactor) > ?factorTolerance ||
                            ABS(?failure - ?expectedTorque) > ?torqueTolerance ||
                            ABS(?maximum - ?expectedTorque) > ?torqueTolerance
                        )
                    }
                ") ] ]

sh:sparql [ sh:message Literal("Spindle torque factor and torque results must satisfy the declared blade-failure formula.") ; sh:select Literal("
                    PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
                    PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
                    PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
                    SELECT $this
                    WHERE {
                        $this nltl:bladeExpandedAreaRatio ?earNode ;
                              nltl:propellerBladeCount ?z ;
                              nltl:leadingEdgeChordPortionAtZeroPointEightRadius ?leNode ;
                              nltl:trailingEdgeChordPortionAtZeroPointEightRadius ?teNode ;
                              nltl:extremeIceForce ?forceNode ;
                              nltl:bladeFailureSpindleTorqueFactor ?factorNode ;
                              nltl:bladeFailureSpindleTorque ?failureNode ;
                              nltl:maximumSpindleTorque ?maximumNode .
                        ?earNode qudt:numericValue ?ear .
                        ?leNode qudt:numericValue ?le .
                        ?teNode qudt:numericValue ?te .
                        ?forceNode qudt:numericValue ?force .
                        ?factorNode qudt:numericValue ?factor .
                        ?failureNode qudt:numericValue ?failure .
                        ?maximumNode qudt:numericValue ?maximum .
                        BIND((4.0 * ?ear) / xsd:decimal(?z) AS ?ratio)
                        BIND(0.7 * (1.0 - (?ratio * ?ratio * ?ratio)) AS ?rawFactor)
                        BIND(IF(?rawFactor < 0.3, 0.3, ?rawFactor) AS ?expectedFactor)
                        BIND(IF(?le > (0.8 * ?te), ?le, (0.8 * ?te)) AS ?chord)
                        BIND(?chord * ?expectedFactor * ?force AS ?expectedTorque)
                        BIND((ABS(?expectedFactor) * 0.000001) + 0.000000001 AS ?factorTolerance)
                        BIND((ABS(?expectedTorque) * 0.000001) + 0.000000001 AS ?torqueTolerance)
                        FILTER(
                            ABS(?factor - ?expectedFactor) > ?factorTolerance ||
                            ABS(?failure - ?expectedTorque) > ?torqueTolerance ||
                            ABS(?maximum - ?expectedTorque) > ?torqueTolerance
                        )
                    }
                ") ] ]

Required change: Make the SPARQL constraint select only cases that establish applicability, so the branch conforms when the category/date combination is outside category A or B on or after the threshold, while preserving xsd:date validation for every present constructionDate value. | [LOGIC] MainShape/sh:or first branch/loadingConditionCase/sh:node/sh:or: The residual-stability-factor alternative is allowed regardless of alternativeInstrumentApplicable. Required change: Guard the residualStabilityFactorSI=1 branch with alternativeInstrumentApplicable=false, leaving the alternative branch as alternativeInstrumentApplicable=true together with alternativeInstrumentResidualStabilityStatus=true.
source_oracle_rationale: Applicable ship has no loading-condition readiness case.

exception_message: [LOGIC] MainShape/sh:sparql[1] assignment-coverage constraint: The constraint claims to enforce assignment for every person on board but only compares personOnBoard with a count of distinct persons found in qualifying reified assignment statements. It never identifies the actual persons on board, so the count can be satisfied by different or unrelated persons while an onboard person lacks assigned thermal-protection equipment. Required change: Bind the actual persons-on-board manifest and require each such person to have a qualifying assignedThermalProtection value, rather than relying on an aggregate count. | [OWNERSHIP_PATH] MainShape/sh:sparql[1] assignment-coverage constraint, '?person ?shipMembershipPath $this': The person-to-ship relationship uses an unconstrained variable predicate and assumes the reverse direction from person to ship. This can match arbitrary predicates and does not establish that the matched persons are members of the ship's persons-on-board manifest. Required change: Use the authoritative manifest ownership/path relationship and direction for persons on board, then evaluate assigned thermal protection for those persons.
source_oracle_rationale: Thermal protection not assigned.

exception_message: [APPLICABILITY] MainShape/sh:sparql/sh:select: The applicability condition requires only that nltl:tankType exists, but never restricts its value to the two required tank categories; instead it tests unrelated rdf:type assertions. A tank with an arbitrary tankType value can therefore be treated as applicable, while a required tank lacking that extra property can be skipped. Required change: Encode the tank-type applicability directly through the canonical nltl:tankType representation, explicitly limiting it to oil residue tanks and oily bilge water holding tanks, and remove the unconstrained existence check and unrelated substitute classification. Required change: Ensure each applicable tank cannot bypass validation when its individual capacity is absent or unusable; enforce the required capacity input before evaluating the >30 m3 exception.
source_oracle_rationale: Applicable tank separation below 0.76 m.
